1: God has given us everything needed for a godly life, so that we may share in the divine nature. Add virtue, knowledge, self-control and love to your faith. Peter was an eyewitness of the Transfiguration. No prophecy of Scripture is a matter of private interpretation.
Grace makes us sharers in God's own life. Scripture is to be read with the Church, not on our own authority.
2: False teachers will arise, bringing in destructive ideas and exploiting people out of greed. God judged the angels who sinned, the world of Noah and Sodom, and he knows how to rescue the godly. These teachers promise freedom while being slaves of corruption.
A promise of freedom that leads back into sin is a trap. God's judgement on evil is certain.
3: Scoffers ask where the promised coming is. With the Lord one day is as a thousand years. He is patient, not wanting anyone to perish. The day will come like a thief, and we look for new heavens and a new earth. Paul's letters contain things hard to understand, which some twist.
God's delay is mercy. Peter already ranks Paul's letters with "the other Scriptures".
